title: Private control plane: mTLS session leak during orchestrator upgrade caused proxy ephemeral port exhaustion and request throttling
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: During a rolling orchestrator upgrade to private-2026.03, control plane proxy processes began accumulating half-closed mTLS sessions and leaked ephemeral port reservations. Over a ~30 minute window this manifested as large numbers of TIME_WAIT/FIN_WAIT sockets and ephemeral port exhaustion on the control plane proxies in 3 customer clusters. Symptoms included: failed gRPC streams to agents, elevated client connection latency, and automatic throttling/fallbacks in the serving runtime. Impact: 4 customers on Dedicated Private tier experienced degraded control-plane operations (API timeouts, slow leader election) for up to 47 minutes. Root cause hypothesis: a combination of an orchestrator-side TLS library regression (connection re-use disabled by default in new build), a timing regression in the proxy's connection reaper, and a misconfigured ephemeral port-range + aggressive max_fds on the proxy side produced a session leak and prevented sockets from being reused. Key contributing factors: 1) upgrade batch size and schedule (large parallelism across AZs) 2) no preflight test for MTLS keepalive behavior during upgrades 3) limited observability on ephemeral port utilization for private control plane proxies. Detection timeline: - 2026-02-27 03:15 UTC: Canary cluster logs show rising FIN_WAIT sockets - 2026-02-27 03:42 UTC: Alert: control-plane grpc error rate > baseline - 2026-02-27 03:50 UTC: Rollout paused; initial mitigation applied (reduce orchestrator parallelism, restart proxies) - 2026-02-27 04:05 UTC: Partial recovery observed; decision to roll back change to TLS library in canary - 2026-02-27 04:30 UTC: Full rollback to previous orchestrator build completed across affected clusters Recovery: Immediate mitigations were effective (rolling restart of proxy processes and ephemeral port-range expansion). After rollback, socket counts returned to normal and API error rates dropped to baseline. Action items (short term, owners, ETA): 1) Hotfix PR to reinstate connection pooling/reuse defaults in orchestrator TLS client: owner Michael Hart, ETA 2026-03-05. 2) Proxy connection reaper hardening: add aggressive TIME_WAIT sweep and memory-safe fd handling; owner Priya Singh, ETA 2026-03-12. 3) Add automated preflight upgrade test that verifies mTLS handshake reuse under simulated upgrade parallelism: owner SRE team (lead: Javier Alvarez), ETA 2026-03-22. 4) Update runbook with ephemeral port exhaustion checks and an automated remediation script (ephemeral port-range adjust + proxy restart): owner Reliability Docs (author: Aisha Kapoor), ETA 2026-03-08. 5) Post-release canary policy change: reduce parallelism and increase rolling delay for control plane upgrades by default; owner Product Ops (Elena Wu), ETA 2026-03-10. Longer-term mitigations: - Implement runtime telemetry for ephemeral-port and TIME_WAIT saturation per-proxy, surfaced in Console with alerting thresholds. Owner: Observability (Danielle Morris), ETA Q2 2026. - Audit all TLS library upgrades with explicit conn-reuse behavioral test coverage. Owner: Security/Applied ML infra, ETA Q2 2026. Links & artifacts: - Rollout job: https://ci.internal.redwood/runs/43219 - Canary metrics dashboard: https://dashboards.internal.redwood/controlplane/canary-ephemeral-2026-02-27 - Hotfix PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/912 - Incident notes and raw tcpdump excerpts: internal drive link (redacted) Postmortem status: preliminary root cause identified; working through code-level fixes and additional telemetry. Will update after hotfix and post-deploy verification.
